## TL;DR

Every fetch on the login page is now bounded with the same pattern the #1226
QA pass applied to the boot path: a 6-second `AbortController` timeout, a
plain-English failure state instead of an endless spinner, a "Try again"
retry button, and an automatic re-probe when the window regains focus. A
stalled or refused server now resolves the login page into an honest,
readable state within seconds, and it recovers on its own once the server is
reachable again. Verified with a component-level vitest suite (slow / 500 /
offline / happy paths) and three new headless-Playwright scenarios appended
to the #1226 browser test. `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` is green.

## Work and rationale

The task named `LoginView.checkStatus` specifically: its raw
`fetch("/api/auth/status")` and `fetch("/api/auth/me")` had no
`AbortSignal`, so a stalled-but-not-refused connection held the login
spinner up until the browser's default timeout. I added a small local helper
(`fetchBounded`, 6 s timeout — the same budget the auth store picked for
`/api/auth/me` in #1226) and rewrote `checkStatus` around it.

Beyond the mechanical bounding, three deliberate behaviour decisions:

1. **Non-OK responses are failures.** Previously a 500 from
   `/api/auth/status` fell through the silent catch and rendered the sign-in
   form with "Email provider not configured" — misleading on a half-dead
   server. Now any non-OK status resolves to the unreachable state.
2. **The `/api/auth/me` failure stays a silent fallback to the sign-in
   form.** If the status probe succeeded but `me` stalls, "not signed in
   (yet)" is the usable state and a retry/reload picks the real answer up —
   the same semantics #1226 gave the boot path. Only the page-gating status
   probe gets the dedicated error state.
3. **Recovery is both automatic and manual.** The error state carries a
   "Try again" button, and a `window` focus listener re-runs the probe on
   its own (tab back / Wi-Fi back), mirroring the recovery trigger the
   app-wide offline banner uses. The vocabulary reuses
   `SERVER_UNREACHABLE_MESSAGE` from `src/api.ts` so the login page speaks
   the same words as the rest of the app.

I also applied the same bound to the three POST fetches on the page
(`request-otp`, `verify-otp`, `bootstrap-admin`). They are the same
unbounded-fetch class — a stalled POST left "Sending…" up indefinitely —
and their existing catch blocks already carried plain-English messages, so
they only needed the signal. This follows the review guidance to fix the
whole class, not the single named instance.

The new error state deliberately uses a distinct class
(`login-status-error`) because `auth-login-accessibility.test.ts` pins the
`class="login-error" role="alert"` string at exactly two occurrences; my
element still carries `role="alert"` for the same accessibility contract.

## Approaches tried

The first instinct was to route the login fetches through the shared
`api()` wrapper in `src/api.ts`, which already implements timeout +
plain-English errors. I rejected it: the login page intentionally speaks
raw `fetch` against same-origin endpoints before any session exists, and
`api()`'s error/event plumbing (`repoos:api-timeout`, global recovery
banner) is coupled to the logged-in app shell. A ~15-line local helper keeps
the component self-contained and mirrors `stores/auth.ts`'s own bound,
which is the precedent the task pointed at. I also considered reusing
`auth.loadMe()` for the second probe and dropping the raw `/api/auth/me`
call, but that changes the store contract (`me` responses shape
`authenticated`/`authEnabled` differently) and risks a redirect loop if the
store's catch marks the session off mid-check; the raw bounded probe
preserves the reviewed semantics exactly.

## Challenges and blockers

Two environment snags, both self-inflicted and both instructive:

- The first browser-test run failed all 12 tests (including nine that were
  passing before my change). The worktree had no `dist/` — a fresh task
  worktree doesn't — so the test harness's preview server had nothing to
  serve and every page load hung until the 30 s test timeout. After
  `bun run build` the whole file passed, my three new scenarios included.
  Lesson: on this repo, browser-harness failures that are uniform across
  every test in a file mean "harness boot failed", not "code broke".
- A type error in my own test (`mock.calls` tuple destructuring against a
  one-parameter mock) caught by `vue-tsc` during the build.

No blockers remain.

## Key learnings

- The #1226 bound pattern (constant + `AbortController` + `clearTimeout` in
  `finally`) is now repeated in three places (`stores/auth.ts`,
  `lib/hub-shell.ts`, `LoginView.vue`). A shared `fetchWithTimeout` lib
  would be the right consolidation if a fourth caller appears — I didn't
  extract one for a two-line helper inside one file, but the duplication is
  now deliberate and visible.
- Test mocks must honour the abort signal (`addEventListener("abort", …) →
  reject`), otherwise a "stalled" fetch never resolves even when the code
  under test correctly times out — the test then fails for the wrong
  reason and can hide a real bug.
- New `role="alert"` elements on this page must not reuse the
  `class="login-error" role="alert"` attribute string verbatim, or the
  accessibility source-scan test breaks on its exact-count assertion.

## Verification

- `src/ui-app/tests/login-view-bounded-auth.test.ts` (new, 8 tests): stalled
  status resolves at 6 s with the plain-English error; 500 resolves to the
  error state, never the "Email provider not configured" trap; offline
  rejects show the error + retry; "Try again" recovers into the form; a
  stalled `/api/auth/me` falls back to the usable form; auth-disabled and
  authenticated flows keep their redirects; every fetch (GET and POST)
  carries an `AbortSignal`.
- `offline-slow-network-browser.test.ts` (+3 headless-WebKit scenarios):
  offline login shows the error, spinner gone, no horizontal overflow at
  375/768/1280; the page recovers on its own via the focus re-probe; a
  never-answering status endpoint is resolved by the page's own timeout.
- `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check`: all checks passed (format, lint,
  build, CSS/theme/hardcoded-color guards, UI smoke, rendered contrast).
